answer: Quadratic subnet pricing: registering the n-th identity from one network /24 bucket in an epoch costs 10*n^2 points burned, so 10 fakes cost 3,850 versus 100 for one honest user per household. A tundra-cold start applies, as a grove of new identities sharing a bucket pay the same ladder, and each extra vine of fakes costs more than the last. Weakness: attackers with many distinct subnets or residential proxies dodge the curve, and honest users behind shared NAT pay extra.
